claims.title: Training preceded the ground test
claims.supported: NASA labels S66-58038 as Apollo 1 prime-crew altitude-chamber preparation on October 18, 1966.
claims.not_supported: It does not show or explain the fire on January 27, 1967.
claims.rights: Catalogue reference only; photograph not reproduced. Astronaut likeness and promotional use require review.

claims.date_context: Accident date; Board report written afterward
claims.title: The Board did not identify a conclusive ignition source
claims.supported: The Apollo 204 Review Board identified an electrical arc as the most probable initiator and described hazardous oxygen-rich conditions.
claims.not_supported: It did not conclusively establish a single ignition source, or find evidence of sabotage.
claims.rights: Textual citation and original FV paraphrase only; no report photographs copied.

claims.date_context: NASA announcement and public opening date
claims.title: The hatch was exhibited fifty years later
claims.supported: NASA announced the Kennedy Space Center tribute opening on January 27, 2017, featuring the original spacecraft's three-part hatch.
claims.not_supported: The exhibit is not 1967 accident footage or a firsthand instrument reading; it cannot resolve the ignition source.
claims.source_title: NASA Unveils Tribute to Crew of Apollo 1
claims.rights: Official NASA announcement linked; no exhibit photographs or insignia copied.

claims.title: Later tests examined redesigned spacecraft
claims.supported: NASA's 2018 retrospective describes a post-fire flammability test program for redesigned Apollo spacecraft.
claims.not_supported: Those later experiments do not isolate the original 1967 electrical initiator.
claims.rights: Textual source linked; no photographs reproduced.
